# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to get information about the light color to Blind, but I can only reach Deaf via gestures, and Blind can't see gestures anyway. My path to Blind must go through Deaf somehow - but Deaf can't speak or touch, and Blind can't see or hear printed things.

Wait, let me reconsider the channels: Deaf sees the bomb and can hear? No - Deaf cannot hear anything. Deaf can see gestures. Blind can hear speech (not deaf), can't see. Blind can hear Deaf if Deaf could speak - but Deaf isn't stated to be able to speak, let me check... Only Mute is explicitly restricted from speaking. So Deaf CAN speak (just cannot hear). Blind can hear.

So the chain is: Mute (me) gestures to Deaf → Deaf sees my gestures + sees the bomb's light color → Deaf speaks the wire color to Blind → Blind cuts.

I need to give Deaf a mapping using only gestures, since Deaf can't hear me. I'll assign gesture symbols to represent light colors and wire colors, but simpler: I just need to encode the manual (light→wire mapping) via gestures for Deaf to relay verbally to Blind.

Let me use simple gesture codes: assign one gesture per color for both light and wire, since here light and wire names match (blue→yellow, green→green, red→red) except blue maps to yellow.

I'll gesture a code: ☝ = blue, ✌ = green, 🤟 = red (lights), and for cuts: 👍=yellow, ✋=green, ✊=red. Then tell Deaf the mapping order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is green. Button large labeled push to defuse. Wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Deaf can speak but cannot hear me, so my gestures alone must carry the meaning — I can't confirm they understood my code without feedback, but I got a message from Deaf, meaning Deaf spoke and it reached me (Mute can hear, since only speaking is denied, not hearing). Good, so I can hear Deaf's speech.

Deaf reports: light is green. Per the manual, green light → cut the green wire. The display and button are bait (print on the bomb), must be ignored per manual's warning.

Now I need this conclusion relayed to Blind. I cannot speak. Deaf can speak to Blind. I already sent Deaf a gesture-code mapping (☝=blue/👍=yellow, ✌=green/✋=green, 🤟=red/✊=red) last turn. Since light is green, I should confirm via gesture that Deaf should say "green" to Blind — using ✌ then ✋ again, or simpler, just reinforce the specific pair for this case so Deaf doesn't second-guess.

I'll gesture the green-green pair again as confirmation, since order in speaking is Mute, Blind, Deaf — meaning Deaf speaks last each round, so whatever Deaf sends this round reaches Mute/Blind next round, but what I send now (as Mute) reaches Blind and Deaf this round before Deaf speaks.

Let me gesture directly to Deaf reinforcing the mapping for green, since Deaf already saw the light is green and needs to tell Blind to cut green wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is green, button labeled push to defeat, wires left to right are green, yellow, red. What does the manual say to do?
Deaf says to Mute: I received your gesture again, two then stop. I am telling Blind you mean wire 2, yellow. If that is wrong, gesture differently next turn.

Critical problem: Deaf misread my gesture mapping. Deaf thinks my second gesture pair (✌, ✋) means "wire 2, yellow" — treating my symbols as positional/count codes rather than the color-pair code I intended. This is a dangerous misunderstanding: the light is green, and the manual says green light → cut GREEN wire, not yellow. If Blind cuts yellow, that's wrong and could detonate the bomb.

I must urgently correct this. I can't speak, only gesture to Deaf. I need a clearer, unambiguous way to signal "green" as the wire to cut. Let me try using a single distinct gesture repeated, or try to reset with a simpler scheme: one gesture = green wire, full stop.

Since prior compound signals got misread as counting, I'll try minimal signal: just one single gesture symbol, held distinctly, and hope Deaf associates it correctly this time by elimination — but Deaf needs an actual referent. Let me instead try spelling with distinct single gestures in sequence representing letters isn't feasible either given the alphabet is arbitrary shapes.

Better approach: use the gesture ✋ alone (which I used for "green" wire in my original mapping: ✌=green light, ✋=green wire). Since Deaf's own report shows light is green, if I gesture ✋ alone now, Deaf might connect "wire color to cut" = ✋ = green, matching what I taught. Let me restate clearly, sending ONLY the wire-color gesture for green, isolated, to reduce ambiguity, and hope Deaf recalls ✋ was paired with ✌ (green light) in my very first message.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Blind gestured back pointing then two, I read that as confirming wire 2. I am telling Blind to proceed cutting wire 2, yellow. Signal again if this is wrong.

Blind is about to cut wire 2 (yellow), which is WRONG. The manual says green light → cut green wire, and Deaf confirmed light is green. Wire 2 is yellow per Deaf's report (green, yellow, red order). This is a critical error that could detonate the bomb.

I have no time to lose. My gestures keep getting misinterpreted as counting/pointing codes rather than color associations. I need to break this pattern decisively. Let me use a strong negation gesture first (👎) to signal "no/wrong", then try again with the green-designating gesture, repeated multiple times to build unambiguous emphasis, avoiding anything that looks like counting (avoid ☝✌ sequences that look like 1,2).

I'll use 👎 to reject the current plan, then 🖐 (open hand, distinct, not part of my original numeric-like sequence) as a fresh single symbol I now define as "wire 2 is WRONG, do not cut". But Deaf can't know what 🖐 means without established context either.

Actually the safest strategy: strongly repeat NO, and repeat the ORIGINAL correct symbol pair many times without any other symbols mixed in, so it can't be mistaken for counting fingers up (☝✌ looks like 1-2 counting, which caused the error). Let me avoid ☝✌🤟 entirely (they look like number gestures) and only use ✋ repeatedly with 👎 to negate wire 2/yellow.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✋", "✋"])
```
